tips: Drink at least 8 glasses of clean, boiled or filtered water every day to stay energized.

child: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months provides ideal nutrition and immunity for your baby.
Ensure complete and timely immunizations according to the national schedule to protect against major childhood diseases.
During diarrhea, start ORS solution immediately along with zinc supplements to prevent dehydration.
Practice regular handwashing with soap before feeding your child and after using the toilet.
pregnant: Take iron-folic acid (IFA) tablets daily after meals to prevent anemia and ensure healthy fetal growth.
Eat nutrient-rich foods including green leafy vegetables, milk, lentils, and seasonal fruits regularly.
Complete all 4 recommended antenatal care (ANC) checkups with your ASHA worker and PHC.
Watch for danger signs: severe headache, blurred vision, swelling of hands/face, or vaginal bleeding — contact your ASHA immediately.
chronic: Take your prescribed blood pressure and diabetes medicines regularly without skipping doses.
Reduce salt, sugar, and processed foods in your daily meals; drink plenty of clean water.
Engage in 30 minutes of brisk walking or light exercise daily to support heart and blood sugar control.
Attend regular health checkups and monitor blood pressure and blood sugar at your nearest sub-center.
general: Maintain personal hygiene and wash hands thoroughly with soap before meals and food preparation.
Drink clean, boiled, or filtered water to protect against waterborne infections and typhoid.
Eat a colorful, balanced diet with local grains, pulses, and seasonal fresh vegetables.
Contact your local ASHA worker promptly if anyone in your household experiences persistent fever or cough.
